sources.what: Avizienis, Laprie, Randell, Landwehr — 'Basic Concepts and Taxonomy of Dependable and Secure Computing', IEEE TDSC 1(1), 2004. The canonical engineering taxonomy that owns 'fault / error / failure'.
sources.why: The word pair error/failure is not this practice's to define fresh. Dependability theory defines them as stages of a causal chain: a fault (adjudged cause) activates an ERROR (the part of system state that may cause a failure), which becomes a service FAILURE when it reaches the service interface and the delivered service deviates from correct. Cited so this night's cut (error = present-wrong, failure = absent-expected) is placed against the field's cut (causal stage), not offered as if the terms were free.

definitions_as_read.failure: an event that occurs when the delivered service deviates from correct service
definitions_as_read.error: that part of the total state of the system that may cause a subsequent failure / the detectable part of the system state
definitions_as_read.fault: the adjudged or hypothesized cause of an error

sources.what: Georges Canguilhem, 'The Normal and the Pathological' (Le normal et le pathologique). The philosophy of the norm that owns error-as-relation-to-a-norm.
sources.why: Grounds the S26 subtraction (error = a norm imposed on a difference) in the field rather than in this practice's coinage. Canguilhem's 'normativity' — the living being's capacity to institute new norms — is the concept behind Simondon's genetic point (the failure creates the standing-apart from which a norm can be set). Consulted; confirms S26, does not move it.
